title: A method for generating a cybersecurity report
originalTitle: Un metodo per eseguire la generazione di un report di sicurezza informatica
description: Machine-learning pipeline that merges auditors’ vulnerability notes, rewrites them in report style and assigns a severity, automating security audit reports.
seoDescription: Granted Italian patent IT202400016273A1 by Christian Vari: an ML pipeline that merges auditors’ notes, writes the findings and rates their severity.
summary: A method and system that automatically turn the findings of a security source code audit into the final report. Several researchers annotate the same code; the system merges their notes for each part of the code into one consistent description, rewrites it in professional report style and assigns a severity, then produces the client-ready document.
The work a quality-assurance team does by hand (aggregating notes, resolving disagreements about severity, rewriting and formatting) becomes a fast, reproducible pipeline.
problem: In a security audit, each researcher reviews the code independently and leaves notes on a pull request in the project's git repository. The same vulnerability is often described several times, in different words and with different severity ratings.

Before anything reaches the client, a quality-assurance team has to collect every note, reconcile discrepancies, settle on a severity (informational, minor, major or critical) and rewrite everything to the company's reporting standard. The process is slow, depends on scarce specialists and is hard to reproduce.

pipeline.name: Embedder
pipeline.text: Reads the downloaded pull request, with its notes, from the database and turns it into numerical vectors the models can process.

pipeline.name: Seq2Seq LSTM with attention
pipeline.text: Combines every note that refers to the same section of code into a single, coherent description. Trained on a general English corpus and on historical audit data.

pipeline.name: Transformer
pipeline.text: Rewrites each merged description in the technical, impersonal style of a security report: where the issue is, why it happens, its consequences and the recommendation. Fine-tuned on more than a thousand archived vulnerability descriptions.

pipeline.name: BERT classifier
pipeline.text: Classifies every finding as informational, minor, major or critical. Fine-tuned on descriptions with known severities and on public vulnerability databases (CVEs).

pipeline.name: Formatter
pipeline.text: Places the final descriptions and severities into the company's report template and exports a PDF the client can download.

architecture.name: Frontend
architecture.text: Web app where a user requests a report by pointing at a git repository and pull request.

architecture.name: Orchestrator
architecture.text: Coordinates the flow, saves each request and its progress to the database and notifies the other services through an event channel.

architecture.name: Parser
architecture.text: The only component with repository access. Downloads the pull request with its notes and converts it to JSON.

architecture.name: Analyzer
architecture.text: Runs the machine-learning pipeline and stores the final descriptions and severities.

architecture.name: Formatter
architecture.text: Generates the PDF report from the template.

benefits: Reports in a fraction of the time, without a manual consolidation step
Independent, scalable services: each can be replicated, restarted or stopped on its own
Repository access isolated in a single component
